entities.name: Pedro Afonso, conde de Barcelos
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Pedro Afonso, born in 1287, was the most prominent illegitimate son of King Denis of Portugal and Grácia Froes, and a pivotal figure in the development of Portuguese historiography and genealogy during the late Medieval period. As the 3rd Count of Barcelos from 1314, he wielded significant influence within the Portuguese court, but his enduring legacy stems from his meticulous compilation of historical and genealogical works that shaped the understanding of Iberian noble lineages and early Portuguese history. His contributions provided critical primary source material for subsequent chroniclers and offered a unique window into the social and political structures of 14th-century Portugal.

Elevated to the prestigious title of Count of Barcelos on May 1, 1314, Pedro Afonso participated actively in the political intrigues and military campaigns of his era, often finding himself at odds with his half-brother, King Afonso IV. Despite periods of exile and reconciliation, his true genius lay in his scholarly pursuits. He authored the monumental *Livro de Linhagens* (Book of Lineages), a comprehensive genealogical treatise detailing the noble families of Portugal and Castile, which remains an indispensable source for medieval Iberian prosopography. Furthermore, he translated and compiled the *Crónica Geral de Espanha de 1344*, a vast historical narrative that synthesized earlier Iberian chronicles and presented a unified history of the peninsula from its mythical origins to his own time, thereby significantly expanding the historical consciousness of the Portuguese court.
